(a) The cited lines drift: fallbackModel sits at packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:194 (not :189) and PiAgent.getFallbackModel at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6256-6258 (not :6234). Only the absence claim is exact -- MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534 does carry availableModels and enforceAvailableModels and does not carry fallbackModel. (b) The load-bearing half of the claimed our-state is false. fallbackModel does NOT live in 'user-editable workspace defaults'. ~/.nessy-agent/config-defaults.json is overwritten from the app bundle's apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json on EVERY launch -- syncConfigDefaults, storage.ts:198-226, comment at :160 'Always writes on launch to ensure defaults are up-to-date with the running version' -- and writeFileSync(CONFIG_DEFAULTS_FILE, ...) at :209/:218/:225 is the only writer in the repo. So a user cannot set it at all, and a hand-edit of the JSON is clobbered at next start. (c) Verifying the consequence separately from the identifier, per the repo's own recurring-false-positive shape: 'an admin cannot pin the fallback' does not hold in the sense the sentence guards. The doc exception exists because fallbackModel is an ARRAY that would otherwise merge -- settings.md:277, 'Unlike most array settings, this key does not merge across settings files: the highest-precedence file that defines it supplies the entire chain.' Our value is a scalar with exactly one source and no lower layer, so 'the managed value replaces lower layers rather than merging' is already trivially the effective behaviour, and the value is in fact pinned harder than Claude's model allows -- fixed by the shipped bundle and re-asserted every launch, unoverridable by any user. The genuine residue is much narrower than the claim: the key cannot be changed through the managed-policy channel without rebuilding. And that residue rides on a shape mismatch already recorded three times -- f106, f226, f242 all file our scalar single-retry knob against Claude's ordered three-model chain. f113 restates that same underlying divergence against a precedence sentence that cannot bite a single-source scalar. Not one of the nine inert-worklist section 3 owner decisions: item 2 there covers availableModels/enforceAvailableModels enforcement placement, not fallbackModel. Refuted on the evidence, not as a recorded decision.
correctedState: fallbackModel is absent from MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS (managed-policy.ts:501-534), so an administrator cannot set it through the managed-policy channel (managed-policy.json or the delivered payload) without rebuilding the app. But it is equally unreachable from below: it is read only by PiAgent.getFallbackModel (pi-agent.ts:6256-6258) from ~/.nessy-agent/config-defaults.json, a file syncConfigDefaults overwrites from the bundled apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json on every launch (storage.ts:198-226), with no setter, no RPC, no UI and no per-workspace override anywhere in the repo. There is therefore no lower layer for a managed value to replace and no user override to defeat -- the doc's merge carve-out, which settings.md:277 ties to fallbackModel being an array, is vacuous against our scalar. The real fallbackModel divergence is its arity (one model, one retry, gated on FALLBACK_MODEL_RETRY_ERROR_CODES, default '' meaning disabled) versus Claude's ordered chain of up to three, and that is already filed as f106, f226 and f242.
